title: Workload Suite v0 (Draft) — Q1 2026 Perf Baselines
content:
Doc status: v0 draft for review. This is the working definition of the workload suite we will use to establish Q1 2026 locked baselines for the Serving Runtime. It includes workload IDs, target token distributions, concurrency regimes, cache scenarios, streaming vs non-streaming modes, and example prompt templates.

IMPORTANT: This suite intentionally does not include any raw customer prompts or unique customer strings. Anything labeled “derived” is from aggregated/anonymous production signals (histograms and ratios) and then re-implemented with synthetic prompt templates.

Owners / sign-off targets
- Workload representativeness: Claire Dubois + Jonas Weber
- Scheduler realism / batching stress: Sofia Ivanova + Lena Fischer
- Variance budgets / trial counts: Sana Farid + Sean Gallagher
- Telemetry correctness: Nadia Rahman
- Suite plumbing / versioning: Marcus Reed + Rina Kobayashi

Goals
1) Provide a small, stable set of workloads that capture the majority of performance-sensitive behavior in production: prompt-length mix, output lengths, streaming behavior, concurrency/bursts, cache hit rates, and multi-tenant mixing.
2) Ensure workloads are reproducible across runs (seeded generation, locked templates, pinned distributions, explicit warmup).
3) Be explainable: each workload is designed to isolate or stress specific runtime components (prefill vs decode balance, scheduler backpressure, KV cache, batching heuristics).

Non-goals
- Not attempting to reproduce any single customer workload exactly.
- Not optimizing for adversarial prompts or red-team content.
- Not encoding product/business semantics in prompts (prompts are purely to create token shapes and compute patterns).

Definitions (v0)
- prompt_tokens (PT): tokens in request input.
- output_tokens (OT): tokens generated.
- TTFT: time to first token as recorded by server timestamps (streaming) and client wall-clock (validation harness). For baseline, TTFT uses server timestamp definition (see telemetry validation notes).
- TPOT: time per output token during decode; computed over streamed chunks or over full completion for non-streaming.
- Cache scenarios:
  - cold: cache cleared between trials or distinct prefixes to avoid reuse.
  - warm-prefix: controlled prefix reuse across a defined hit rate (e.g., 30%/70%).
  - warm-kv: repeated conversation turns that reuse KV state (where supported by scenario).

Synthetic vs derived labels
- synthetic: distribution chosen by us (e.g., uniform/normal mixtures) to hit stress patterns.
- derived (aggregated): token length histograms, streaming share, and concurrency patterns based on aggregated production telemetry (no prompt text, no customer IDs, and bins are coarse). We use these only to select mixture weights and ranges.

Traffic shape knobs (as implemented in benchmark-lab)
- Mode: streaming | non_streaming
- Inter-arrival: poisson | fixed | burst (ramp + spike)
- Concurrency target: fixed N | ramp N0→N1 | sawtooth
- Prompt length distribution: mixture of lognormals (bin-matched)
- Output length distribution: capped lognormal or fixed
- Stop condition: max_tokens only (avoid content-dependent early stops)
- Multi-tenant mixing: A/B tenant IDs with independent rate limits (simulated), or separate queues if supported by runner

Workload list (v0)

WS-01: Chat — “Short prompt, medium output” (derived)
Purpose: Baseline for common chat behavior; mainly decode-bound; validates streaming TTFT instrumentation and stable batching.
Mode: streaming
Prompt tokens (PT): mixture (approx): 60% in [40–120], 30% in [121–350], 10% in [351–700]
Output tokens (OT): mixture: 50% in [120–300], 40% in [301–700], 10% in [701–1200]
Concurrency: fixed 32 and fixed 128 variants (two runs under same workload ID, separate “concurrency” dimension)
Inter-arrival: poisson to hold concurrency
Cache: cold (0% prefix reuse)
Notes: Derived mixture weights from aggregate PT/OT histograms and streaming ratio. Emphasis on tail latency under mild-to-moderate queueing.
Example prompt template(s):
- System: “You are a helpful assistant. Follow the user’s instructions. Keep the response structured.”
- User: “Summarize the following meeting notes into: (1) Decisions, (2) Open Questions, (3) Action Items. Notes: {{synthetic_paragraph_3_to_8_sentences}}”
- User alt: “Rewrite the following text to be clearer without changing meaning: {{synthetic_paragraph}}”
Generation notes: synthetic_paragraph generated from a fixed vocabulary + deterministic pseudo-sentences to avoid semantic early stopping.

WS-02: Chat — “Long prompt, short output” (synthetic)
Purpose: Prefill-heavy workload; stresses kernel selection for long prefill and scheduler fairness when prefill dominates.
Mode: streaming
PT: fixed 6,000 (context window permitting); otherwise 4,000 for smaller-context variants (runner chooses based on model context)
OT: fixed 128
Concurrency: fixed 16 and fixed 64
Inter-arrival: fixed to hold concurrency
Cache: cold
Example prompt:
- User: “Given the following policy document, extract a table with columns [Topic, Requirement, Exception]. Document: {{synthetic_policy_doc_6k_tokens}}”
Notes: The “policy doc” is synthetic headings + bullet patterns; do not include real policy text.

WS-03: Coding assistant — “Medium prompt, medium output, non-streaming” (derived)
Purpose: Non-streaming latency/throughput baseline for completion mode; helpful for customers using non-streaming API (batch jobs, eval pipelines).
Mode: non_streaming
PT: mixture: 50% [200–600], 40% [601–1400], 10% [1401–2400]
OT: mixture: 60% [200–500], 30% [501–900], 10% [901–1500]
Concurrency: fixed 64
Inter-arrival: poisson
Cache: cold
Example prompt:
- “Write unit tests for the following function. Use a table of test cases first, then provide test code. Function signature and description: {{synthetic_function_spec}}”
Notes: “synthetic_function_spec” is a deterministic template with placeholder variable names.

WS-04: RAG-ish Q&A — “Repeated prefix / warm-prefix cache” (synthetic)
Purpose: Controlled cache hit rate; isolates prefix caching/KV reuse behavior and checks correctness of cache state annotations.
Mode: streaming
PT: prefix block ~1,500 tokens + query tail ~80 tokens
OT: fixed 256
Concurrency: fixed 64
Inter-arrival: poisson
Cache: warm-prefix at target hit rates 30% and 70% (two runs)
Mechanics:
- Maintain a library of 200 prefixes (synthetic “knowledge base excerpt”).
- Requests sample prefixes with Zipf parameter s=1.1 to create realistic skew.
- Query tail always unique to prevent full-response caching.
Example prompt:
- Prefix: “Knowledge base excerpt:\n{{synthetic_kb_excerpt}}”
- Tail: “Question: {{synthetic_question}}\nAnswer with citations to section headers.”
Notes: This workload is synthetic but designed to approximate repeated-context RAG patterns without storing any customer docs.

WS-05: Burst concurrency — “Queueing + tail protection” (derived)
Purpose: Stress scheduler under bursty arrivals; validates load-shedding hooks and p99 control mechanisms.
Mode: streaming
PT: mixture: 70% [50–200], 20% [201–700], 10% [701–1800]
OT: mixture: 70% [80–250], 25% [251–700], 5% [701–1500]
Concurrency profile: ramp 16→64 over 60s, then spike to 256 for 30s, then settle to 64 for 120s
Inter-arrival: burst (scripted)
Cache: cold
Acceptance notes (v0): We will track queue wait distribution, batch composition over time, backpressure events, and error responses (429/503) during spike. Derived from aggregate “burstiness index” and observed spike durations; no direct customer mapping.
Example prompt:
- “Draft a concise response (<= 8 bullets) to this customer email: {{synthetic_email_paragraph}}. Keep it professional.”

WS-06: Mixed tenants — “Latency-sensitive + throughput tenant on shared pool” (synthetic)
Purpose: Model multi-tenant interference, fairness, and batching interactions.
Mode: streaming
Tenant A (latency tier): PT [50–250], OT [80–250], concurrency fixed 32, p95 TTFT priority
Tenant B (throughput tier): PT [200–1200], OT [300–900], concurrency fixed 128, best-effort
Inter-arrival: poisson per tenant
Cache: cold
Mix: 40% tenant A requests, 60% tenant B
Metrics to watch: tail TTFT for tenant A, throughput for tenant B, batch composition and prefill/decode utilization.
Example prompt:
- Tenant A: “Summarize: {{synthetic_paragraph_short}}”
- Tenant B: “Generate a detailed outline for a technical blog post based on: {{synthetic_topic_brief}}”

WS-07: Long-context streaming — “Stress TTFT + first-chunk behavior” (synthetic)
Purpose: Known sensitive area for instrumentation and first-chunk timestamp; used to guard against TTFT regressions in streaming for large PT.
Mode: streaming
PT: fixed 12,000 where supported; else max allowable minus safety margin (runner chooses PT = min(12000, ctx_limit-1024))
OT: fixed 256
Concurrency: fixed 8 and fixed 16
Inter-arrival: fixed
Cache: cold
Notes: This workload is intentionally small concurrency due to memory pressure. Validate that TTFT is defined consistently (server-side first token emission), and ensure no chunking artifacts.
Example prompt:
- “Given the following transcript, produce: (1) a 10-line summary, (2) a list of named entities, (3) 5 follow-up questions. Transcript: {{synthetic_transcript_long}}”

WS-08: Microbatch pressure — “Many small requests” (synthetic)
Purpose: Exercise batching heuristics, kernel launch overhead, and scheduler overhead with small PT/OT.
Mode: non_streaming
PT: fixed 32
OT: fixed 32
Concurrency: fixed 512 and fixed 1024 (hardware permitting)
Inter-arrival: poisson
Cache: cold
Example prompt:
- “Convert the following tag list into JSON: {{synthetic_tags_10}}”
Notes: This is intentionally “unrealistic text” but realistic shape for high-QPS small-completion use cases (classification-like). Useful for regression detection.

Prompt set generation (v0)
- All templates are deterministic and parameterized.
- A single suite seed controls:
  - selection among templates
  - synthetic text generation
  - prefix library content (for WS-04)
- Prompts must be:
  - content-agnostic with max_tokens stop (avoid early stop due to “done”)
  - stable tokenization across versions as much as possible (avoid exotic unicode)
  - free of sensitive or customer-like strings

Token distribution implementation notes
- We represent distributions via either:
  - explicit mixture bins with weights, or
  - parametric lognormal defined in token space with truncation.
- For derived workloads, weights/ranges are selected to match coarse bins (e.g., 0–64, 65–128, 129–256, …) from aggregate telemetry.
- The runner should log realized PT/OT histograms per trial to confirm it hit targets (and to detect drift due to tokenizer/model changes).

Cache scenarios details
- cold: ensure unique prefixes per request; flush cache state between trials where feasible.
- warm-prefix: control hit rate using prefix sampling distribution; tag each request with cache_expected=true/false and compare to runtime cache annotations.
- (future) warm-kv: multi-turn conversations; requires explicit support for reusing KV state across turns within a single session.

Measurement notes (what the suite expects the harness to emit)
Per request (min required):
- request_id, workload_id, trial_id, seed
- model_id, quant_profile, hardware_sku, region
- mode (streaming/non)
- prompt_tokens, output_tokens
- ttft_ms, tpot_ms
- end_to_end_latency_ms
- error_code (if any)
Scheduler / runtime metrics (required for explainability in baseline runs):
- queue_wait_ms histogram (or quantiles)
- batch_size distribution over time
- prefill/decode utilization (GPU) and token counters
- backpressure events, shed events (if enabled)
- cache_state annotation (miss/hit + relevant counters)

Open questions / TODOs for v1
1) Model coverage: do we need separate WS-01 variants per context length tier (e.g., 8k vs 32k) or do we parameterize PT caps and treat that as a dimension?
2) Streaming chunking: standardize chunk size for baseline runs to reduce variance in TTFT/TPOT (align with runtime defaults or force fixed chunk config?).
3) Multi-region noise: should WS-05 burst runs be excluded from “global comparisons” and treated as per-region only due to fleet variance?
4) Derived distributions refresh: do we re-derive mixture weights quarterly, while keeping workload IDs stable? (Proposal: keep IDs stable; allow weights update only via ADR + baseline bump.)
5) Warm cache methodology: ensure warm-prefix does not accidentally become warm-everything due to reuse patterns; validate hit rates from telemetry.

Proposed acceptance criteria for adopting suite v0 into baseline runs
- Workloads implemented in benchmark-lab with schema validation (PR-412/419 lineage)
- For each workload: realized PT/OT distributions within tolerance (TBD; propose +/- 5% per bin for bins >10% weight)
- Repeatability: p50 and p95 stable within variance budget across 5 trials on a single region/hardware
- Explainability: scheduler metrics present and can account for p99 movements in at least one induced regression experiment

Notes on confidentiality / data handling
- No raw production prompts. No customer identifiers. No copying from support tickets.
- “Derived” means only that we looked at aggregated numeric summaries (length histograms, concurrency patterns, streaming ratio). Those summaries are coarse-binned and not keyed by customer.
- Any future request to incorporate additional production signals requires Security/Privacy review and must be documented in an ADR.

Next steps
- Review with Runtime + SRE + Evals (target: end of week 2).
- Convert this doc into a Confluence “canonical workload suite spec” once sign-offs land.
- Once stable: lock prompts/templates and release as workload-suite v0.1 tag with seeds + artifact packaging (ENG-4823).

Change log
- 2026-01-09: initial draft created (Claire)
- 2026-01-28: added WS-06 mixed tenants and clarified derived vs synthetic labeling (Claire/Jonas)
- 2026-02-14: expanded cache notes + TTFT instrumentation expectations (Nadia/Marcus)
